t: Aim and plan of the session
n: In this session we will study phenothiazine derivatives. Aminazine, diprazine, tizercin and other phenothiazine derivatives have toxicological and narcological significance. The aim is to learn preliminary testing of urine for phenothiazine derivatives with the FPN test, their isolation, and their detection by TLC and by UV spectrum. The plan has four parts: first, preliminary testing of urine; second, isolation from blood and urine; third, TLC; fourth, identification of aminazine, diprazine and tizercin by colour reactions and UV spectrum.

As a result of the session you should be able to do the following. First, evaluate the result of the FPN test in urine by colour: dark red-pink or light red-pink. Second, isolate phenothiazines from blood and urine with n-heptane in an alkaline medium. Third, evaluate the TLC spots by Rf st and colour relative to the aminazine reference, using Table 16. Fourth, confirm aminazine, diprazine and tizercin by colour reactions and UV spectrum maxima.

List of reagents and equipment. For preliminary testing of urine, a mixture of 10% sulphuric acid and 5% iron (III) chloride, or FPN reagent, is used. For isolation, a 50% sodium hydroxide solution, pH=13, n-heptane with 3% isoamyl alcohol, a water bath and a separating funnel are needed. For TLC, a standard sample of aminazine, that is the reference, chloroform, and, as developing agent, concentrated sulphuric acid and ethanol 1:9 or Marquis reagent are taken. For re-extraction and purification, 0.5 M sulphuric acid, 10, 10, 10 and 5 ml, and ethanol and 25% ammonia 1:1 are used.

Safety rules. The student brings rubber gloves, a wipe and a face mask to the laboratory work. The examination is carried out in rooms with ventilation and a fume cupboard, which are locked and sealed after the work. Objects from infectious persons, that is those with tuberculosis, hepatitis or AIDS, arrive in a special container and are marked in the documents.

Classification of phenothiazines. By 1945, highly active compounds had been obtained by replacing the hydrogen on nitrogen with alkylaminoalkyl radicals. Phenothiazine itself is not used in medicine now. By chemical structure there are three groups. The aliphatic derivatives include aminazine, propazine and levomepromazine. The piperazine derivatives include meteperazine, etaperazine and triftazine. The piperidine derivatives include thioridazine and periciazine. The first group is sedative, the second stimulating, and the third weaker antipsychotics without hypnosedative effect.

Toxicological and narcological significance. Some phenothiazine derivatives potentiate the effect of narcotic and intoxicating substances. Aminazine potentiates the effect of hypnotics, barbiturates, narcotics, analgesics and local anaesthetics. More than 20 metabolites of aminazine have been identified: sulphoxidation, demethylation, N-oxidation, hydroxylation. Because a small part is excreted in the urine unchanged, aminazine can be determined in urine directly.

Key numbers for aminazine. The daily dose of aminazine ranges from 0.075 g to 0.6 g. Treatment may last from 3-4 weeks to 3-4 months. More than 20 metabolites of aminazine have been identified. The metabolites of aminazine and tizercin form conjugates with sulphuric and glucuronic acids. For tizercin, the share in urine is given as about 10%.

t: Preliminary testing of urine: the FPN test
n: Preliminary testing of urine, that is the FPN test, is carried out in two ways. In the first method, 1 ml of reagent is added to 1 ml of urine; the reagent is prepared from 60 ml of 10% H2SO4 and 20 ml of 5% iron (III) chloride. If phenothiazine derivatives are present, a dark red-pink colour forms. In the second method, that is with FPN reagent, 1 ml of reagent is added to 1 ml of urine; the reagent consists of 5 ml of 5% FeCl3, 45 ml of 20% HClO4 and 50 ml of 50% HNO3. In this method a light red-pink colour forms.

Evaluating the FPN test result. If no colour forms, it can be concluded that phenothiazine derivatives are absent. If the reaction is positive, to confirm their presence they are isolated from blood and urine by liquid-liquid extraction and determined by other methods. Remember: propazine gives a pink-violet colour with FPN reagent; salicylates and other co-extractive substances interfere.

The procedure for isolation from blood and urine. 10 ml of urine and 2 ml of blood, in separate vessels, are brought to pH=13 with 50% NaOH and heated for 10 minutes. The cooled hydrolysate is extracted twice, 20 ml each time, with n-heptane containing 3% isoamyl alcohol. The extract is combined, washed with water and divided in two: one part for TLC, the other for identity and quantity.

t: Isolation from blood and urine: the numbers
n: Remember the key numbers of isolation. Urine 10 ml, blood 2 ml. NaOH solution 50%, medium pH=13. Heating for 10 minutes on a boiling water bath. The cooled hydrolysate is extracted twice, 20 ml each time, with n-heptane containing 3% isoamyl alcohol. The extract is divided into two equal parts: for TLC, and for identity and quantity.

The first part of the Salomatin method works with acidified alcohol. The object is soaked for 2 hours in a 10% alcoholic solution of oxalic acid, repeated 3 times. The alcoholic extracts are evaporated at 40 °C to a thick syrup; foreign substances are precipitated with 96% ethyl alcohol. The residue is dissolved in hot water and acidified with a 5% solution of oxalic acid to pH=2-3. It is then extracted with diethyl ether.

General steps of the Salomatin method. First, soaking: with 10% alcoholic oxalic acid solution, 3 times for 2 hours. Second, evaporation at 40 °C to a thick syrup. Third, precipitation: 96% alcohol, then dissolving in hot water to pH=2-3. Fourth, the ether layer: in the acidic medium barbiturates pass into it, and it is discarded. Fifth, alkalinisation: 50% NaOH to pH=13, ether 3 times. Sixth, re-extraction: with 0.5 M H2SO4, 10, 10, 10 and 5 ml.

The second part of the Salomatin method is alkaline extraction. The ether layer from the acidic medium is used to detect barbiturates or is discarded. The aqueous solution is brought to pH=13 with 50% NaOH and extracted 3 times with diethyl ether. The phenothiazines are re-extracted from the ether with 0.5 M sulphuric acid, 10, 10, 10 and 5 ml. The resulting solution is sent for analysis.

Preparing the sample for TLC. Part of the isolate is evaporated to dryness in a stream of hot air, and the residue is dissolved in 0.2-0.5 ml of chloroform. The solution is applied with a capillary tube to the start line of 2 TLC plates. Alongside the sample, a standard sample of aminazine, that is the reference, or a solution of the suspected phenothiazine is always spotted.

TLC chromatographic systems. First system: benzene, dioxane, 25% ammonia solution in the ratio 60:35:5. Second system: ethyl acetate, acetone and a 1:1 mixture of 25% ammonia with ethyl alcohol in the ratio 50:45:4. The spots are detected by spraying with a mixture of concentrated sulphuric acid and ethanol 1:9 or by applying a drop of Marquis reagent.

Let us sum up the TLC systems. System 1: benzene, dioxane, 25% ammonia 60:35:5; system 2: ethyl acetate, acetone, ammonia-alcohol 50:45:4. For aminazine and propazine, a freshly prepared benzene-dioxane-25% ammonia 70:20:5 system is used. For tizercin, a mixture of ammonia-ethanol 1:1, ethyl acetate and acetone 4:90:45 is used.

Table 16 gives the TLC results. Rf st is given relative to the aminazine spot, that is the value for aminazine is 1. The spot colour is the same with sulphuric acid and ethanol 1:9 and with Marquis reagent. Aminazine: Rf st 1 and 1, colour dark red. Diprazine: 0.74 and 2.9, dark red. Levomepromazine, that is tizercin: 1.56 and 1.87, blue. Etaperazine: 0.34 and 0.48, dark red. So tizercin is distinguished by its blue colour, the others by red or dark red.

t: Evaluating the TLC result and purification
n: Evaluating the TLC result and purification. In the evaluation, besides Rf st, attention is also paid to the formation of other spots. If there are additional spots, the second part of the heptane aliquot is purified by TLC. The spot zone is located by applying reagent only to the reference zone; the sorbent is scraped off and eluted with ethanol and 25% ammonia 1:1. The eluate is filtered and evaporated to dryness; qualitative and quantitative analysis is carried out.

Properties of aminazine. The chemical name is 2-chloro-10-(3-dimethylaminopropyl)phenothiazine hydrochloride; synonyms: chlorpromazine, chlorazine, Largactil, plegomazine. A white or faintly pinkish fine crystalline powder; very hygroscopic, darkening in sunlight. It dissolves well in water, ethyl alcohol and chloroform, and is practically insoluble in diethyl ether. In an alkaline medium it dissolves well in organic solvents.

Let us look at the effects of aminazine by group. Central effect: a strong sedative effect on the central nervous system, relaxes skeletal muscles, consciousness is preserved. Potentiation: potentiates the effect of hypnotics, barbiturates, narcotics, analgesics and anaesthetics. Other effects: a strong antiemetic effect, relieves hiccups; it has a hypothermic effect.

Colour reactions of aminazine. With Mandelin reagent a green colour forms first, then red on standing. With Dragendorff's reagent an amorphous precipitate forms first, then quadrangular brown crystals appear. With Marquis reagent a green colour forms first, then red-pink on standing. With concentrated acids: H2SO4 gives a scarlet colour, HNO3 red-pink, and HCl first pink, then red.

Detecting aminazine by TLC and UV spectrum. In TLC a freshly prepared benzene-dioxane-25% ammonia 70:20:5 system is used; the developing agent is Marquis reagent or sulphuric acid and ethanol 1:9. If aminazine is present, a pink-violet colour forms at an Rf of about 0.93. UV spectrum: in 0.1 M sulphuric acid 255 and 307 nm; its main metabolite, the sulphoxide, 239, 274, 300 and 341 nm. The quantity is determined by UV spectrophotometry or by the absorbance of the red colour produced with concentrated H2SO4, that is on the photoelectrocolorimeter.

Diprazine, also called pipolphen, promethazine, protazine, is a white crystalline powder; it dissolves well in water at 1:60, in ethyl alcohol at 1:9 and in chloroform at 1:2. It is an antihistamine with a sedative effect and potentiates the effect of narcotic, hypnotic, neuroleptic and analgesic substances. One of the main metabolites is the sulphoxide; it can be detected in urine even after 14 days. Diprazine is also excreted in the urine in the unbound form; it is isolated from the biological object like other phenothiazines.

Let us compare aminazine and diprazine. Aminazine: chlorpromazine, Largactil; hygroscopic, darkens in light; on TLC Rf=0.93; UV spectrum in sulphuric acid 255 and 307 nm. Diprazine: pipolphen, promethazine; a sedative antihistamine; on TLC Rf=0.72; UV spectrum in sulphuric acid 249 and 300 nm. The sulphoxide of diprazine is detected in urine even after 14 days.

Let us compare the solubility ratios. Diprazine dissolves in water at 1:60, in ethyl alcohol at 1:9, in chloroform at 1:2; it is practically insoluble in ether. Haloperidol dissolves in ethanol at 1:50, in chloroform at 1:20, in diethyl ether at 1:200, in methanol at 1:55. Droperidol dissolves in ethanol at 1:140, in chloroform at 1:40, in ether at 1:500.

Detecting diprazine. With Mandelin reagent a green colour forms first, then scarlet. With concentrated acids: H2SO4 gives a scarlet colour, HNO3 first light red, then scarlet, HCl reddish pink, then scarlet-pink; Marquis reagent gives a scarlet colour. On TLC Rf=0.72. UV spectrum: in water-ethanol 1:1, 252 and 301 nm; in 0.1 M H2SO4, 249 and 300 nm. The quantity is determined from the UV spectrum by the spectrophotometric or photoelectrocolorimetric method.

Let us compare the UV maxima. Aminazine in 0.1 M H2SO4 255 and 307 nm; its sulphoxide 239, 274, 300, 341 nm. Diprazine in water-ethanol 1:1 252 and 301 nm; in 0.1 M H2SO4 249 and 300 nm. Tizercin in ethyl alcohol 255 and 310 nm; in 0.1 M HCl 251 and 302 nm.

Tizercin, also called levomepromazine, levopromazine, methotrimeprazine, is a white crystalline powder; it dissolves well in ethyl alcohol, diethyl ether and chloroform, and poorly in water. It has adrenolytic, antihistamine and analgesic effects; a rapid and strong sedative. It is metabolised by oxidation, hydroxylation, sulphoxidation and N-demethylation; about 10% is excreted in the urine. It is isolated from the biological object in the same way as aminazine.

Distinguishing from other phenothiazines. Propazine gives a pink-violet colour with FPN reagent; on TLC Rf=0.71 in the 70:20:5 system. Etaperazine gives a dark red colour with concentrated H2SO4; on TLC Rf=0.32. Periciazine has weak antipsychotic activity. Chromatographic and spectral methods are used to distinguish them.

Detecting tizercin. With Marquis reagent a bluish red colour forms, with Frohde reagent a reddish bluish colour. If Mandelin reagent is added, cooled, and then concentrated sulphuric acid is added, a red-pink colour forms. In TLC the developing agent is a 50% solution of sulphuric acid in alcohol; if the plate is heated for 3-5 minutes at 100 °C, a red spot forms. UV spectrum: in ethyl alcohol 255 and 310 nm, in 0.1 M HCl 251 and 302 nm; the quantity is determined spectrophotometrically or on the photoelectrocolorimeter.

Methods of quantitative analysis. Aminazine is determined from the UV spectrum or by the absorbance of the red colour produced with concentrated H2SO4, that is on the photoelectrocolorimeter. Propazine is determined on the photoelectrocolorimeter or by UV spectrophotometry, based on the colour produced with FPN reagent. Diprazine and tizercin are determined from the UV spectrum by the spectrophotometric or photoelectrocolorimetric method. As a sensitive method, gas chromatography-mass spectrometry may also be used.

Interpreting the result. The methods of isolating phenothiazines and the identity reactions are similar; therefore TLC, GLC, HPLC and spectral methods are used to distinguish them. In TLC, besides Rf st, additional spots are also taken into account. In Table 16 tizercin is distinguished by a blue spot, that is levomepromazine, while aminazine and diprazine are distinguished by a dark red spot.

The case task is taken from the textbook. Urine was brought to the forensic chemical examination; its colour was orange, and in the preliminary analysis the urine turned red. Question: for which substances must the analysis be carried out, and why is the urine red? The direction is as follows: in the FPN test, a dark red-pink or light red-pink colour points to phenothiazine derivatives.

Let us compare haloperidol and droperidol. Haloperidol is a strong neuroleptic; if the dose is exceeded, it ends in death in 15-22% of cases. It gives a yellow colour with Marquis reagent, orange with Frohde reagent and dark yellow with Mandelin reagent; UV 246 nm. Droperidol is rapid and short-acting; it takes effect in 3-10 minutes, and 10% is excreted unchanged. It gives yellow with Marquis and Frohde reagents and yellow-green with Mandelin; UV 247 and 276 nm. UV is measured in 95% alcohol for haloperidol and in formic acid for droperidol.

The steps of isolating haloperidol and droperidol. First, alkalinisation: 50% NaOH is added to 10 ml of urine and 2 ml of blood to bring the pH to 13. Second, heating for 30 minutes on a boiling water bath. Third, the cooled hydrolysate is extracted three times with ethyl acetate. Fourth, the extracts are filtered through anhydrous Na2SO4 and evaporated. Fifth, the residue is dissolved in 95% alcohol. Sixth, TLC is carried out: under UV 254 nm and with Dragendorff's reagent.

Determining the quantity of droperidol by the methyl orange method. To a solution of droperidol in HCl, 12 ml of acetate buffer, pH=3.5, 2 ml of methyl orange and 5 ml of chloroform are added and shaken. The chloroform layer turns yellow; the absorbance is measured at 400 nm in a 10 mm cuvette. The linear range of determination is 1-10 μg/ml.

Review questions. First: how is the isolation of phenothiazine derivatives from physical evidence carried out? Second: explain the reactions of preliminary testing of urine for phenothiazine derivatives and their significance. Third: how is TLC analysis of phenothiazine derivatives isolated from urine carried out? Fourth: how is the quantity of phenothiazine derivatives determined?

Conclusion. The FPN test in urine is a preliminary examination: if there is no colour, there is no phenothiazine; if positive, it is confirmed by other methods. Isolation from blood and urine is with n-heptane at pH=13; on TLC, Rf st and spot colour are evaluated relative to the aminazine reference. Aminazine, diprazine and tizercin are confirmed by colour reactions and UV spectrum; the quantity is determined by UV or the photoelectrocolorimeter.
